title: Janax y Razar: un sistema operativo, un idioma y un ensamblador propios para un razonamiento artificial que piensa con melodías
description:
Janax is a hand-written operating system, language and assembler (all in assembly, no third-party engines) built to host Razar, an artificial reasoning system whose single judge is compression (two-part MDL). Version 4.01 (versions follow prime numbers; 401 after 397): her reader reads in pieces of 100 KB, and the kernel lets her read the system. Each reading reads one piece of her shelf, at most 100 KB cut at the first line end after, and keeps where the next begins (as Razar's Quijote was measured in pieces of 100 KB); the three pieces of a 296 KB book add up to exactly the words and lines of reading it whole. The kernel now splits the host's known folders: AppData and ProgramData stay closed (secrets live there); inside Windows and Program Files it no longer asks that the folder need no administrator rights and that the user own the file (hidden, system and dot names stay out). Kernel host-watch tests: 96 passing, 3 failing, identical to before. Not yet: the piece reader was not seen finishing inside her body (tested with the standalone reader), and the cause of her reader's crash since v3.79 is still unknown. Documentation is in Spanish.

Janax es un sistema operativo, un idioma y un ensamblador escritos a mano en assembler, hechos para alojar a Razar. v4.01: su lectora lee de a pedazos de 100 KB. Prototipo de investigación.
